Not bad but different
Sep 2026 • Family
All Seasons Buffet is a bit different from the usual buffet concept.

You don’t walk around choosing seafood from a big display. Instead, you choose a set menu depending on how much lobster you want: no lobster, half a lobster, one whole lobster, or unlimited lobster. After that, the dishes keep coming to your table, more like a Brazilian churrascaria than a traditional buffet.

Personally, I wouldn’t really call it a buffet in the usual sense. If you are used to buffets in Australia, New Zealand, Europe or other parts of Oceania, this feels quite different.

The price is high, even by international standards, and the variety is not huge. On the positive side, the presentation is very good. The dishes are served nicely and clearly a lot of effort goes into how the food looks.

As for the taste and value for money, that is very subjective.

For me, it is around 3 out of 5. Not because the food was bad, but because I simply prefer a real buffet where I can walk around, see everything, and choose exactly what I want instead of waiting for dishes to be brought to the table.
